body: [{"streamId":"01a0d518-39eb-7338-a696-16d48a56f013","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskAdded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0d518-39eb-7338-a696-16d48a56f013\u0022,\u0022ProjectId\u0022:\u002201a077d8-2b7d-75a0-a0eb-c3deff5f2a4e\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:\u0022A dispatched session runs at the effort level the node configures, so a model whose own default is medium (Claude Opus 5.5) builds, fixes and reviews at high when the operator asks for high\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022h9k config set --effort \\u003Clow|medium|high|xhigh|max\\u003E stores the level in config.json under hall9k; h9k config show and h9k daemon status print it with its origin the way default-model is printed; the word default clears it; any other value is rejected with the five accepted names\u0022,\u0022When the level is set, ClaudeSettingsFile.Build writes effortLevel with that value into every dispatched session\\u0027s settings file (build, fix, review, verify, final pass, synthesis, publication, courier, pr-review alike); when it is not set the key is absent and the file is byte-for-byte what it is today, so existing ClaudeSettingsFileTests still pass unchanged\u0022,\u0022A running daemon binds the level at startup like every other DaemonOptions value; h9k config set --effort prints the same restart note default-model prints\u0022,\u0022The docs page that lists h9k config set\\u0027s model knobs gains the effort knob beside them, with one sentence saying why it exists: a headless session ignores the owner\\u0027s user-level effortLevel and honors the --settings file, and Claude Opus 5.5 defaults to medium where earlier Opus models defaulted to high\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Evidence gathered 2026-09-24 on this Windows node (Claude Code 2.1.282, model claude-opus-5-5[1m]): two plain claude -p runs with effortLevel high in ~/.claude/settings.json recorded effort medium in their transcripts; three runs whose --settings file carried effortLevel high, modelSettings.\\u003Cmodel\\u003E.effortLevel high, or env CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL high all recorded effort high, as did --effort high. So the daemon\\u0027s generated settings file (Hall9k.Connectors/Prompts/ClaudeSettingsFile.cs, Build) is the one place the level can be carried, and Hall9k.Daemon/Execution/ClaudeExecutor.cs Arguments already passes that file. Follow the DaemonOptions.DefaultModel pattern (Decisions Log #33) for the knob. One node-wide level; per-role effort is out of scope. Prefer effortLevel in the file over the env variable, which hard-locks and cannot be lowered by a session. No em dashes in anything
